title: Inside Turkey-Azerbaijan tensions over headscarves, Armenia and Israel
gist: Turkey and Azerbaijan publicly patched up a rare row over Baku's Sept. 21 school headscarf ban, which led Aliyev to skip the Organization of Turkic States summit in Ankara, but underlying disagreements over Armenia, Israel and domestic interference persist.

insights.claim: Azerbaijan's Sept. 21 school dress code effectively barred headscarves in public schools and drew criticism from lawmakers of Erdogan's AKP.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Religious-identity issues can strain an otherwise tight strategic alliance.

insights.claim: In response to Turkish criticism, Ilham Aliyev skipped the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States held Oct. 30 in Ankara.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: A visible snub signals the depth of the rift.

insights.claim: The crisis eased after Erdogan's Nov. 8 visit to Azerbaijan, after which Aliyev attended COP31 in Antalya on Nov. 11.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Public reconciliation reduces near-term disruption risk to Turkey-Azerbaijan energy and transit ties.
insights.locator: The crisis eased only after Erdogan

insights.claim: The episode exposed simmering disagreements over interference in domestic affairs, relations with Armenia and Baku's close ties with Israel.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Divergence on Israel and Armenia could resurface and complicate South Caucasus connectivity projects.
insights.quote: exposed simmering disagreements over interference in domestic affairs, relations with Armenia and Baku’s close ties with Israel

insights.claim: A Baku think-tank expert noted that while Ankara and Baku have often disagreed, they have rarely traded such public rebukes.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Novelty of public spat suggests structural strain rather than routine friction.
insights.quote: they have rarely traded such public rebukes
